clue.text: Room microphone picking up American Quartet or similar

parts.note: a chamber is a room

indicators.note: to pick something up is to take it in, so one piece gathers another inside itself

parts.note: mic is the short form of microphone
US is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A microphone in a room is recording an American string quartet.
explanation.walkthrough: The microphone takes the American inside it, M-US-IC, which follows the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A string quartet is the classic example of music written for a small ensemble playing in a private room.

clue.text: Like Batman keeping company in New England resort

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: Batman is the Caped Crusader
CO is the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Batman keeping company with holidaymakers at a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like Batman' points to his nickname, the Caped Crusader; the company is tucked in before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Massachusetts peninsula is a well-known summer holiday destination in the north-eastern United States.

clue.text: Performer in part of composition after the opening

indicators.note: what comes after the opening is everything except the first letter, so that letter goes

parts.note: a factor is one of the elements making up a whole

explanation.surface: A musician plays a section of a piece once its introduction is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition' suggests music, but here it means make-up: a factor is a constituent part. Dropping its first letter leaves the performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays roles on stage or screen is one kind of performer.

clue.text: Target certainly reflected in brief highlighted item

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other
something brief is cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a bullet point marks out an item in a list

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: yes, as an emphatic agreement

explanation.surface: A target is certainly shown in a short highlighted item of a report.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'highlighted item' is a bullet point in a list; 'reflected' turns the agreement round before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of a dartboard or archery target is its most prized spot, and the word also stands for the target itself.

clue.text: Organised guy, abandoning university, disposed to roam

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
U is the usual abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A well-organised man drops out of university because he wants to wander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' looks like an anagram signal but is simply RAN, past tense of run; GUY without U gives GY.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides meaning long-limbed, the word has an older sense of inclined to range or wander about.

clue.text: Posh, undiluted beer around Belgium not fit to consume

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: U means upper-class in old British slang
a neat drink has no water added
ale is a beer
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: Strong, posh Belgian beer judged unfit to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a crossword convention from the 1950s U and non-U debate. ALE wraps B to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that cannot be consumed because it is spoiled or unpleasant is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Female depression coming after one new arrival

indicators.note: coming after sets the order, placing the earlier-named words behind the later ones

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N is the abbreviation for new
F is the abbreviation for female
a low is an area of low pressure, a weather depression

explanation.surface: A woman is depressed after having a new baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming after' places the female depression after one new; 'new arrival' looks like a baby, but only 'arrival' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An influx of people, money or water coming in is an arrival in the collective sense.

clue.text: Coat not worthy of additional decoration

parts.note: an animal's fur is its coat
beneath someone, as in 'below one's dignity'

explanation.surface: A coat that does not merit any more embellishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat' is an animal's coat, not a garment; 'below' in the sense of beneath one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy trimming such as a flounce or ruffle on a dress, often in the phrase frills and furbelows.

clue.text: Solid work at university involving reading, perhaps?

indicators.note: to involve is to include within, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: study is what students do
reading is one of the three Rs, so R can stand for it

explanation.surface: Serious university work involves plenty of reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, hence 'perhaps': reading is only one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something strongly built and firm, not easily broken or knocked over.

clue.text: Tantrum before a doctor leaves emergency vehicle in irritation

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking or temper

indicators.note: to leave a place is to depart it, so those letters depart from the word

parts.note: the vehicle that answers a 999 call
A plus MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A patient throws a tantrum before a doctor climbs out of the ambulance, annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: MB (Bachelor of Medicine) is a common crossword doctor; A MB comes off the front of AMBULANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish bad temper and sulky annoyance are the same feeling, so the noun matches irritation.

clue.text: Tragic academic quickly adopting United

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: fast means quickly
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A gloomy professor hastily becomes a Manchester United fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tragic academic' is the scholar of Marlowe's and Goethe's tragedies.
explanation.definitionFit: The learned doctor who sells his soul to the devil is the hero of famous tragedies by Marlowe and Goethe.

clue.text: Reversing, you once nearly hit Bob

indicators.note: to reverse is to go backwards, so the letters are read from the far end
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
struck is the past tense of strike, to hit

explanation.surface: Backing out of a parking space, you nearly hit someone called Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name but is the verb for a quick dip of the knees. YE plus STRUC, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to make a quick bending of the knees as a greeting, which is what a curtsey is.

clue.text: A useless sort, but for a collection of features

parts.note: tool is slang for an idiot
bar means except, as in 'bar none'

explanation.surface: Someone who is hopeless apart from a set of good qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Features' suggests a face or character, but they are software functions; 'but for' and 'bar' both mean except.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, a strip of buttons on screen gathers a program's functions in one place.

clue.text: Birthday drunk seizing mike to deliver wild poem

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it, so one piece is taken into the other
someone drunk stumbles about in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drunk at a birthday party grabs the microphone to recite some wild verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' looks like a microphone but is the phonetic-alphabet M, which joins the letters of the birthday before they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a frenzied Greek hymn to Dionysus, the term now covers any wildly enthusiastic piece of verse.

clue.text: Recommendation to take in particular quiet settlement

indicators.note: taking in means receiving inside, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
own, as in 'my own', means particular to one person
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Advice to someone to choose a particularly peaceful place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' is the adjective sense of own, as in 'a style all its own'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small town or community is one kind of settlement, a place where people have made their homes.

clue.text: High pay, or chap produces dubious works

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated and muddled, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A big salary, or maybe the man himself, lies behind some questionable output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High pay' reads as one phrase, a large salary; 'High' is actually the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Writings of doubtful authorship or authenticity, especially books left out of the biblical canon, go by this collective name.

clue.text: Maybe the end of work involves line for stage production

indicators.note: to involve is to include within, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: pay is what work is for, its end in the sense of purpose
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: The final part of a job may involve lines being learnt for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' means aim or goal, not the last part; wages are one possible goal of work, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama performed in a theatre is a production put on the stage.

clue.text: Journalists heading for Klosters engaged in excellent evening in bar there?

indicators.note: to be engaged in something is to be caught up inside it, so pieces go within another

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, and the 1 is read as the letter I
the press are journalists collectively

indicators.note: a heading is what comes at the top, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Klosters, a Swiss ski resort

explanation.surface: Reporters in Klosters enjoy a great night out in a bar at the resort.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is read as A and I; the 'there' of the definition points back to Klosters, a ski resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term covers the drinking and socialising at a ski resort once the day's skiing is over.

clue.text: Away from university, academic embraces wife

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A lecturer hugs his wife while away from campus.
explanation.walkthrough: In Oxbridge usage you go up to university and come down when you leave, so the definition is the phrase in front.
explanation.definitionFit: British university slang says students are 'down' when they have left or are on vacation from Oxford or Cambridge.

clue.text: Poster put up: "Camouflage fabric"

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up makes it read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an ad is an advertising poster
to mask is to disguise

explanation.surface: A notice goes up advertising camouflage cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Camouflage fabric' look like the poster's words, but only 'fabric' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversible woven textile with a pattern, originally from Damascus, used for tablecloths and furnishings.

clue.text: Get the best of complete component of quadratic equation

parts.note: over means finished
a quadratic contains x to the power two

explanation.surface: Solving a whole quadratic equation to beat the maths problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' suggests the maths technique of completing the square, but it just means finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat or overwhelm someone by greater strength is to get the better of them.

clue.text: Left-wing outfit denying Democrat reparation

parts.note: red is the colour of the political left

indicators.note: to deny is to refuse entry, so that letter is refused a place

parts.note: a dress is an outfit
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A left-wing group refuses a Democrat compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outfit' looks like an organisation, but it is clothing; DRESS loses its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensation or remedy for a wrong suffered is what both nouns describe.

clue.text: Big name from Italy in the sea at Cannes, here in France

parts.note: Cannes lies on the Mediterranean, the Med
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: A celebrity from Italy is swimming off Cannes, here in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At Cannes' suggests the French word for sea, but the sea is simply the Med.
explanation.definitionFit: The banking family who ruled Florence and patronised Renaissance art is among Italy's most famous dynasties.

clue.text: A lot of people regret returning manipulator?

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Many people regret the return of a scheming politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manipulator' suggests a schemer; the question mark signals the literal sense of someone who manipulates muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who kneads and works the body's muscles with the hands does manipulation in the physical sense.

clue.text: Patchy dessert, perhaps unadorned

parts.note: a pie is one kind of dessert
bald means plain, as in a bald statement

explanation.surface: An uneven pudding, maybe served without decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patchy' reads as uneven in quality, but here it describes a coat of irregular colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with irregular black and white patches is described this way, so the coat is patched.

clue.text: Group of soldiers with no working source of philosophy?

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a platoon is a small military unit
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A squad of soldiers without a functioning source of wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a description, not a synonym: one of the founders of Western thought.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian thinker whose dialogues shaped Western thought is a fountainhead of the whole discipline.

clue.text: Chance to unseat head of Government? No great hurry

indicators.note: unseating someone throws them off, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a gamble is a chance taken

indicators.note: the head of anything is its top, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An opportunity to topple the prime minister, though nobody is rushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of Government' looks like the prime minister but is just G, the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely stroll is walking at an easy pace, the opposite of rushing.

clue.text: Some terrific stuff recalled in this genre

definitions.note: the definition includes 'this', pointing back at the terrific stuff

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters are read backwards
some means a part of, so the letters are taken from inside the words

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Remembering great material from a particular kind of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards through 'terrIFIC Stuff' to find the genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a literary and film genre about imagined futures, space and technology.

clue.text: Pause Bill for review? That's likely

indicators.note: something under review is gone over and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Parliament halting a bill so it can be reviewed seems probable.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue: the first part is the fodder and signal, 'That's likely' is the verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Something believable and reasonable enough to seem probably true is what both adjectives describe.

clue.text: Details? Irons out reluctance to act

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in place, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has to iron out every detail is really putting off taking action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irons out' reads as a phrasal verb meaning resolves; split, 'out' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Slowness and a tendency to delay or procrastinate amount to a hesitancy about getting on with things.
